weapons: Martial weapons that have the {@filter Finesse or Light|items|type=martial weapon|property=finesse;light} property

entries: {@i Choose A or B:} (A) {@item Leather Armor|XPHB}, 2 {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, {@item Shortsword|XPHB}, {@item Shortbow|XPHB}, {@item Arrows (20)|XPHB|20 Arrows}, {@item Quiver|XPHB}, {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, {@item Burglar's Pack|XPHB}, and 8 GP; or (B) 100 GP

subclass.name: Scion of the Three
subclassFeatures: Scion of the Three|Rogue|XPHB|Scion of the Three|FRHoF|3|FRHoF
Aura of Malevolence|Rogue|XPHB|Scion of the Three|FRHoF|13|FRHoF

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} and {@skill Stealth|XPHB} are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Rogue level 6, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Sneak Attack
entries: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, and you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.
The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

classFeature.name: Thieves' Cant
entries: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in {@book chapter 2|XPHB|2|Choose Languages}.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of two kinds of {@filter weapons|items|type=simple weapon;martial weapon} of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers} and {@item Shortbow|XPHB|Shortbows}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties} of {@item Scimitar|XPHB|Scimitars} and {@item Shortsword|XPHB|Shortswords}.

classFeature.name: Cunning Action
entries: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}: {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Rogue Subclass
entries: You gain a Rogue subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Rogue levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Rogue level or lower.

classFeature.name: Steady Aim
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 until the end of the current turn.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Rogue levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Cunning Strike
entries: You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove {@dice 1d6} from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.
If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

classFeature.name: Poison (Cost: 1d6)
entries: You add a toxin to your strike, forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
To use this effect, you must have a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB} on your person.

classFeature.name: Trip (Cost: 1d6)
entries: If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

classFeature.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

classFeature.name: Withdraw (Cost: 1d6)
entries: Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in two of your Skill Proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeature.name: Reliable Talent
entries: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Cunning Strike
entries: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Daze (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Devious Strikes
entries: You've practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

classFeature.name: Knock Out (Cost: 6d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or it has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

classFeature.name: Obscure (Cost: 3d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

classFeature.name: Slippery Mind
entries: Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Elusive
entries: You're so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} against you unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of the Night Spirit|XPHB} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Stroke of Luck
entries: You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can turn the roll into a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodthirst
entries: When an enemy you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes damage and is {@status Bloodied|XPHB} after taking that damage but not killed outright, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and {@variantrule Teleportation|XPHB|teleport} to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of that enemy. You can then make one melee attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Dread Allegiance
entries: Choose one of the Dead Three: {@deity Bane|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, {@deity Bhaal|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, or {@deity Myrkul|Faerûnian|FRHoF}. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one type of damage and the ability to cast a cantrip, as detailed in the table below; Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Scion of the Three
entries: {@i Become a Gruesome Agent of Malice}

A Scion of the Three draws power from a group of malevolent gods known as the Dead Three: {@deity Bane|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, deity of tyranny; {@deity Bhaal|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, deity of violence and murder; and {@deity Myrkul|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, deity of death. While some Rogues of this subclass pledge themselves ardently to those three macabre gods, others find themselves thrust on this path by a curse. Either way, a scion's power manifests as various occult gifts, as well as an uncanny talent for striking and terrifying foes.

Scions of the Three are most common in Baldur's Gate, where the Dead Three have long competed for influence over mortal hearts. Underground cults to {@deity Bane|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, {@deity Bhaal|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, and {@deity Myrkul|Faerûnian|FRHoF} often count Scions of the Three among their most useful agents. Outside Baldur's Gate, secular thieves' guilds such as the Shadow Thieves of Amn or Xanathar's guild in Waterdeep might cautiously call on a Scion of the Three to undertake an especially violent contract.

subclassFeature.name: Strike Fear
entries: You gain the following {@classFeature Cunning Strike|Rogue|XPHB|5|XPHB} option.

entries.name: Terrify (Cost: {@dice 1d6})
entries: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While the target is Frightened in this way, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the target.
The {@condition Frightened|XPHB} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Malevolence
entries: You radiate malignant power associated with one of the Dead Three. When you use {@subclassFeature Bloodthirst|Rogue|XPHB|Scion of the Three|FRHoF|3|FRHoF} and teleport, each creature of your choice within 10 feet of either the space you left or your destination space (your choice) takes damage equal to your Intelligence modifier; the damage type is the same as the damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} granted by your choice in the Dread Allegiance feature. Damage dealt by this feature ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Dread Incarnate
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cutthroat
entries: You regain one expended use of {@subclassFeature Bloodthirst|Rogue|XPHB|Scion of the Three|FRHoF|3|FRHoF} when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Murderous Intent
entries: When you roll for your {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|XPHB|1|XPHB} damage, you can treat a roll of a 1 or 2 on the die as a 3.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Trickster
entries: {@i Enhance Stealth with Arcane Spells}

Some Rogues enhance their fine-honed skills of stealth and agility with spells, learning magical tricks to aid them in their trade. Some Arcane Tricksters use their talents as pickpockets and burglars, while others are pranksters.

subclassFeature.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
entries: When you cast {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}, you can cast it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and you can make the spectral hand {@condition Invisible|XPHB}. You can control the hand as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and through it, you can make Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|XPHB|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules as an Arcane Trickster.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three cantrips: {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} and two other cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard} (see that class's section for its list). {@spell Mind Sliver|XPHB} and {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of your cantrips, except {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}, with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of 1st+ Level
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Wizard spells. {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, and {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Rogue, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard spells.

subclassFeature.name: Magical Ambush
entries: If you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition when you cast a spell on a creature, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any saving throw it makes against the spell on the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Versatile Trickster
entries: You gain the ability to distract targets with your {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}. When you use the Trip option of your Cunning Strike on a creature, you can also use that option on another creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Thief
entries: You gain the ability to magically steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster.

Immediately after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area of effect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the creature to make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC equals your spell save DC. On a failed save, you negate the spell's effect against you, and you steal the knowledge of the spell if it is at least level 1 and of a level you can cast (it doesn't need to be a Wizard spell). For the next 8 hours, you have the spell prepared. The creature can't cast it until the 8 hours have passed.
Once you steal a spell with this feature, you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Assassin
entries: {@i Practice the Grim Art of Death}

An Assassin's training focuses on using stealth, poison, and disguise to eliminate foes with deadly efficiency. While some Rogues who follow this path are hired killers, spies, or bounty hunters, the capabilities of this subclass are equally useful for adventurers facing a variety of monstrous enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Assassin's Tools
entries: You gain a {@item Disguise Kit|XPHB} and a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, and you have proficiency with them.

subclassFeature.name: Assassinate
entries: You're adept at ambushing a target, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Initiative
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls.

entries.name: Surprising Strikes
entries: During the first round of each combat, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. If your Sneak Attack hits any target during that round, the target takes extra damage of the weapon's type equal to your Rogue level.

subclassFeature.name: Infiltration Expertise
entries: You are expert at the following techniques that aid your infiltrations.

entries.name: Masterful Mimicry
entries: You can unerringly mimic another person's speech, handwriting, or both if you have spent at least 1 hour studying them.

entries.name: Roving Aim
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} isn't reduced to 0 by using Steady Aim.

subclassFeature.name: Envenom Weapons
entries: When you use the Poison option of your Cunning Strike, the target also takes {@damage 2d6} Poison damage whenever it fails the saving throw. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Death Strike
entries: When you hit with your Sneak Attack on the first round of a combat, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), or the attack's damage is doubled against the target.

subclassFeature.name: Soulknife
entries: {@i Strike Foes with Psionic Blades}

A Soulknife strikes with the mind, cutting through barriers both physical and psychic. These Rogues discover psionic power within themselves and channel it to do their roguish work. As a Soulknife, your psionic abilities might have haunted you since childhood, revealing their full potential only as you experienced the stress of adventure. Or you might have sought out an order of psychic adepts and spent years learning how to manifest your power.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Power
entries: You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. It is represented by your Psionic Energy Dice, which fuel certain powers you have from this subclass. The Soulknife Energy Dice table shows the number of these dice you have when you reach certain Rogue levels, and the table shows the die size.

Any features in this subclass that use a Psionic Energy Die use only the dice from this subclass. Some of your powers expend a Psionic Energy Die, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your Psionic Energy Dice are all expended.
You regain one of your expended Psionic Energy Dice when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all of them when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The first time you use this power after each {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you don't expend the Psionic Energy Die. All other times you use the power, you expend the die.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Blades
entries: You can manifest shimmering blades of psychic energy. Whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action or make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB}, you can manifest a {@item Psychic Blade|XPHB} in your free hand and make the attack with that blade. The magic blade has the following traits:
The blade vanishes immediately after it hits or misses its target, and it leaves no mark if it deals damage.

After you attack with the blade on your turn, you can make a melee or ranged attack with a second psychic blade as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on the same turn if your other hand is free to create it. The damage die of this bonus attack is {@damage 1d4} instead of {@damage 1d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Psi-Bolstered Knack
entries: If you fail an ability check using a skill or tool with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended only if the roll then succeeds.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Whispers
entries: You can establish telepathic communication between yourself and others. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose one or more creatures you can see, up to a number of creatures equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and then roll one Psionic Energy Die. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, the chosen creatures can speak telepathically with you, and you can speak telepathically with them. To send or receive a message (no action required), you and the other creature must be within 1 mile of each other. A creature can end the telepathic connection at any time (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Homing Strikes
entries: If you make an attack roll with your {@item Psychic Blade|XPHB} and miss the target, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the attack roll. If this causes the attack to hit, the die is expended.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Teleportation
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you manifest a {@item Psychic Blade|XPHB}, expend one Psionic Energy Die and roll it, and throw the blade at an unoccupied space you can see up to a number of feet away equal to 10 times the number rolled. You then teleport to that space, and the blade vanishes.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Blades
entries: You can now use the following powers with your Psychic Blades.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Veil
entries: You can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature or you force a creature to make a saving throw.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a Psionic Energy Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Rend Mind
entries: You can sweep your Psychic Blades through a creature's mind. When you use your Psychic Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). If the save fails, the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. The {@condition Stunned|XPHB} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend three Psionic Energy Dice (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Fast Hands
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can do one of the following.

entries.name: Sleight of Hand
entries: Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check to pick a lock or disarm a trap with {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB} or to pick a pocket.

entries.name: Use an Object
entries: Take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, or take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to use a magic item that requires that action.

subclassFeature.name: Second-Story Work
entries: You've trained to get into especially hard-to-reach places, granting you these benefits.

entries.name: Climber
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Jumper
entries: You can determine your jump distance using your Dexterity rather than your Strength.

subclassFeature.name: Thief
entries: {@i Hunt for Treasure as a Classic Adventurer}

A mix of burglar, treasure hunter, and explorer, you are the epitome of an adventurer. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you gain abilities useful for delving into ruins and getting maximum benefit from the magic items you find there.

subclassFeature.name: Supreme Sneak
entries: You gain the following Cunning Strike option.

entries.name: Stealth Attack (Cost: 1d6)
entries: If you have the {@action Hide|XPHB} action's {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, this attack doesn't end that condition on you if you end the turn behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover} or {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}.

subclassFeature.name: Use Magic Device
entries: You've learned how to maximize use of magic items, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: You can attune to up to four magic items at once.

entries.name: Charges
entries: Whenever you use a magic item property that expends charges, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 6, you use the property without expending the charges.

entries.name: Scrolls
entries: You can use any {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for the spell. If the spell is a cantrip or a level 1 spell, you can cast it reliably. If the scroll contains a higher-level spell, you must first succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check ({@dc 10} plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell from the scroll. On a failed check, the scroll disintegrates.

subclassFeature.name: Thief's Reflexes
entries: You are adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and your second turn at your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} minus 10.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Petitioner
entries: As a rogue, you know that the path to peace and prosperity is rarely as virtuous as the Vassals of the Sovereign Host claim. Victory must be won by pragmatism, sacrifice, and the blood of those who aren't afraid to get their hands dirty.
Though some Dark Petitioners worship the Dark Six as great leaders to venerate and emulate, many instead appease those powers and turn their attention toward their enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: When you reach 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast cleric spells.

You automatically learn {@spell Guidance|XPHB} and learn two additional cantrips of your choice from the Dark Petitioner list: Dancing Lights, Friends, Message, Resistance, Spare the Dying, Thaumaturgy, True Strike, and Traveler's Enigma. At Rogue level 10, you learn another cantrip from that list.

You know three 1st-level cleric spells of your choice. The number of cleric spells you know increases as you gain Rogue levels. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one cleric spell you know with another spell of your choice from the cleric list for which you have spell slots.
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

subclassFeature.name: Pragmatic Petition
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack on your turn, you can use the Bonus Action granted by your Cunning Action to cast one of your Dark Petitioner cantrips, regardless of its normal casting time.

subclassFeature.name: Azur's Advantage
entries: If you roll a 1 or 2 on one or more of your Sneak Attack dice when dealing damage to a creature that is blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, grappled, incapacitated, poisoned, prone, or restrained, you can reroll those dice and must use the new roll.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow's Veil
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can choose to become invisible to that creature for 1 minute or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early if you deal damage to a creature or force a creature to make a saving throw.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Keeper's End
entries: When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you can steal that creature's soul and keep it joined with your own. While a creature's soul is joined to yours, that creature can be restored to life only by a Wish spell.
When you have to make a death saving throw, you can instead release a soul you have stolen to regain 1 Hit Point.

subclassFeature.name: Grim Surgeon
entries: You've developed a unique familiarity with knives, bodies, and blood in your line of work. A grim surgeon uses medical knowledge and strange blood magic to dismantle foes, restore allies, and control bodies like puppets.

subclassFeature.name: Medic
entries: You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill if you don't already have it, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make using it.
You can use a Bonus Action to magically stabilize an unconscious creature within 5 feet of you.

You can also use a Bonus Action to expend one use of a healer's kit on a creature. When you do, that creature regains hit points equal to 1d4 + your proficiency bonus, and it can't regain hit points from this feature again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Transfusion
entries: Once on each of your turns when you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature that isn't a construct or an undead, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).
When you reach Rogue level 13, you instead gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier. These Temporary Hit Points last until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Field Surgeon
entries: At the start of a Short Rest, you can choose a willing creature within your reach. Roll your Sneak Attack dice and record the result. At the end of the Short Rest, that creature regains Hit Points equal to the total.
Once a creature regains Hit Points from this feature, it can't do so again until it finishes a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Toxic Shock
entries: When you gain Temporary Hit Points from Transfusion, the target of the attack is overcome by sickness. Until the end of its next turn, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it has Disadvantage on the next attack roll or ability check it makes before then.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodbound
entries: Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage to a Beast or Humanoid, you can force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.
On a failed save, that creature is affected by Dominate Beast or Dominate Person, respectively, for 1 minute or until you choose to end the effect.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Highway Rider
entries: {@i A Steed Makes the Best Partner in Crime}

Stalking the backroads, the Highway Rider strikes fear into the heart of every traveler and penny-pinching merchant. They run down their prize astride a swift and loyal steed and then make a quick getaway.

subclassFeature.name: Hair Trigger
entries: You gain proficiency with Blackpowder Pistols.

When you roll Initiative and don't have Disadvantage on that roll, you can immediately take a Reaction to make one weapon or Unarmed Strike attack, move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, have a controlled mount move up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or take the Dodge or Utilize action.

subclassFeature.name: Trusty Mount
entries: You always have {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} prepared. With this feature, you can cast it without a spell slot or components, and Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.
Once you cast the spell this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ride Them Down
entries: You don't need Advantage on the attack roll to use Sneak Attack if you or a controlled mount you ride moved at least 20 feet and you don't have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Horse Lord
entries: You can spend 1 minute grooming and caring for your mount, at the end of which it gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Rogue level.

subclassFeature.name: True Grit
entries: You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws.
When an effect allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a success and only half damage on a failure.

subclassFeature.name: Desperado
entries: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points and not killed outright, you can use your Hair Trigger feature immediately before you fall Unconscious.

subclassFeature.name: Misfortune Bringer
entries: {@i Curse Those You're About to Strike}
You've matched your penchant for illicit activities with the ability to mark your enemies for mishap and misfortune.

subclassFeature.name: Evil Eye
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet to be cursed by your Evil Eye.
While a creature is cursed by your Evil Eye, you can deal Sneak Attack damage to it if you don't have Disadvantage on the attack roll.
The curse lasts for 1 minute or until you curse a different creature.

subclassFeature.name: Misfortunist
entries: You learn two Misfortunes of your choice.
You learn an additional Misfortune when you reach Rogue levels 9, 13, and 17. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one Misfortune you know with a different one.
You have 4 Jinx Points, gaining 2 additional Jinx Points at Rogue level 13. You spend Jinx Points to use Misfortunes and regain all expended Jinx Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
If a Misfortune requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Charisma or Intelligence modifier (your choice) + your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Steal Luck
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet is about to make a d20 Test with Advantage, you can take a Reaction to prevent the roll from being affected by Advantage. When you do, you regain 1 expended Jinx Point.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Curse Caster
entries: You can take a Magic action and spend 3 Jinx Points to cast {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Steal Luck
entries: You can use your Steal Luck feature three times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Phantom
entries: {@i Embrace Death and Wield Ghostly Power}
Some Rogues traverse the veil between life and death, shepherding opponents to the grave and slipping through the world as undetectable as a spirit.

subclassFeature.name: Wails from the Grave
entries: Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature on your turn, you can target a second creature you can see within 30 feet of the first creature.
Roll half the number of Sneak Attack damage dice for your level (round up). The second creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Whispers of the Dead
entries: Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can choose one skill or tool proficiency that you lack and gain it. You lose this proficiency when you use this benefit again to choose a different proficiency.

subclassFeature.name: Tokens of the Departed
entries: The spirits of the dead are drawn to you, and echoes of their past lives magically manifest as soul trinkets. You begin with two soul trinkets, and if you move more than 30 feet from one it teleports back to you.
You can destroy a soul trinket when you deal Sneak Attack damage to immediately use Wails from the Grave without expending a normal use.
While you have at least one soul trinket, you have Advantage on death saving throws and Constitution saving throws.
You can take a Magic action to destroy one soul trinket and cast {@spell Augury|XPHB}, or if you know the associated creature, ask that spirit one question instead.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet dies, you can take a Reaction to gain another soul trinket. You can have up to two at a time, increasing to three at Rogue level 13 and four at Rogue level 17.

subclassFeature.name: Voice of Death
entries: You can cast {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} once without a spell slot, requiring no spell components and using Dexterity as your spellcasting ability for the spell. You regain this use when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
When you cast the spell, you can target one of your soul trinkets from Tokens of the Departed instead of a corpse.

subclassFeature.name: Ghost Walk
entries: As a Bonus Action, you assume a spectral form for 10 minutes or until you end it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you destroy one soul trinket to restore your use.
While in this form, you gain a Fly Speed of 10 feet and can hover.
Attack rolls have Disadvantage against you.
You can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, but you take 1d10 Force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or object.

subclassFeature.name: Death's Friend
entries: When you use Wails from the Grave, you can deal the feature's Necrotic damage to both the first and the second creature.
When you roll Initiative, if you have no soul trinkets remaining for Tokens of the Departed, you gain one.

subclassFeature.name: Sanguine Thief
entries: {@i Eliminate Your Prey with Blood Magic}
Sanguine Thieves are assassins who harness the power of Sangromancy to fuel their abilities, finding new ways to use the blood they see all too frequently in their line of work.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast Wizard spells, as well as spells from the Sangromancy school. All Sangromancy spells and cantrips are treated as Wizard spells for the purposes of this subclass.
You know three cantrips from the Wizard spell list and Sangromancy list. When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip.

You prepare the list of level 1+ Wizard spells available to you with this feature, starting with three 1st-level Wizard spells. The number of prepared spells increases as you gain Rogue levels, and whenever you gain a Rogue level you can replace one prepared spell with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.
Intelligence is your spellcasting ability, and you can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for these spells.

subclassFeature.name: Stolen Power
entries: You draw magic from blood, represented by your Sangromancy Dice. You have a pool of d8s equal to the number of Sneak Attack dice shown for your Rogue level.
You can spend Sangromancy Dice instead of Hit Dice when you cast Sangromancy spells.
You regain all expended Sangromancy Dice when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Steal Blood
entries: When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can restore 1 Sangromancy Die.
If you are Bloodied, instead of restoring 1 Sangromancy Die you can immediately roll the die and regain Hit Points equal to the roll's total.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Bloody Blades
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend up to 2 Hit Dice or Sangromancy Dice to create a number of daggers equal to the number of dice spent. Each dagger counts as an Arcane Focus for your Sanguine Thief spells, and you can cast spells with Somatic components even if you wield them.

When you score a Critical Hit with one of these daggers, you can cause it to deal extra Necrotic damage equal to a number of d8s equal to the number of Hit Dice or Sangromancy Dice spent on the feature.
The daggers last until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodstitch
entries: As a Magic action, you can spend 3 Hit Dice or Sangromancy Dice to fling a wave of needle-like blood shards. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
You regain 1 Hit Die or Sangromancy Die of your choice for each creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this feature.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Bloody Exit
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction and spend 5 Hit Dice or Sangromancy Dice to turn into bloody mist. The attack automatically misses you, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you regain your normal form.
As part of this Reaction, you can make one melee weapon attack immediately after you teleport. On a hit, that attack deals an extra 5d8 Necrotic damage.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
